text:
anna: Heads-up — I pushed an RBAC tightening to prod for the scheduler service account a few mins ago. Now seeing some CI/deploy 403s referencing gpu-scheduler-sa. Anyone seeing this too?

devon: Yup, getting 403s when the training job attempts to create pods with nvidia.com/gpu. Errors are during the pod create admission step.

sam: Can you paste the Role/RoleBinding you changed?

anna: Pushed this patch from gitops (shortened):
```yaml
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: gpu-scheduler-restricted
  namespace: ml
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods", "pods/status"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: gpu-scheduler-rb
  namespace: ml
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: gpu-scheduler-restricted
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: gpu-scheduler-sa
    namespace: ml
```
I removed create/patch on pods (assumed scheduler only needed list/watch).

irene: That explains it — scheduler needs to create pods. The scheduler serviceaccount runs the controller that calls the kube API to create pods for scheduled jobs. Removing create was too aggressive.

devon: Audit log snippet from API server (copied):
```
"verb":"create","user":{"username":"system:serviceaccount:ml:gpu-scheduler-sa"},"responseStatus":{"code":403},"reason":"RBAC: access denied"}
```

kms-bot: KMS audit shows no decrypt errors for tokens; service account tokens are valid. This is pure RBAC deny.

sam: Quick triage options:
- rollback to previous RoleBinding (fast)
- add a narrow rule `verbs: ["create"]` for pods only and scope it to the scheduler controller via label selector if possible (safer)
- create a ClusterRole / ClusterRoleBinding if scheduler needs cluster-scoped access (but prefer namespaced Role first)

anna: I'm going to roll back the RoleBinding to the previous commit to restore deploy traffic while we design a least-priv patch. Giving a 5m heads-up.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by anna — gitops deployment queued (#4901). ETA ~2m. :gear:

devon: Thanks. After rollback we should add an integration test that runs `kubectl auth can-i create pods --as=system:serviceaccount:ml:gpu-scheduler-sa -n ml` as part of the PR gate so this doesn't regress.

sam: Also propose we add an admission test that rejects removals of `pods/create` from any SA listed under `apps/schedulers/*` in our config. Prevents accidental least-priv mistakes.

irene: For the follow-up: recommend a rule like:
```yaml
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["create"]
  resourceNames: [] # none, allow scheduler to create any pod but only in ml ns
```
plus a logging annotation on the RoleBinding so audit shows which change introduced the rule.

anna: Rollback completed, deploys recovered. Reopening a PR with updated rules + integration test @sam @devon. I'll tag sec-review.

devon: Great — also please add a note in the incident log: what was changed, why it failed, who reverted, and follow-up owner.

sam: I'll create the follow-up checklist and add a short playbook entry for RBAC rollbacks to speed response next time.

irene: One more ask: when you open the PR, include `kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:ml:gpu-scheduler-sa auth can-i create pods -n ml` output in the PR description so reviewers can validate.

anna: Will do. Closing thread after PR created. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
